newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn crop seen maturing rapidly.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn crop seen maturing rapidly.

text.p: Missouri's corn crop advanced to ninety-four percent dented for the week ended Sunday, up from 60 percent a year ago and ahead of the 82 percent average pace, according to the Missouri Agriculture Statistics Service.
Corn condition was pegged at six percent poor, 25 percent fair, 51 percent good and 18 percent excellent.

Ninety-six percent of the soybean crop was setting pods, five days ahead of last year and the same as the average pace. Twelve percent of the crop was turning color and the crop was just beginning to drop leaves.
Soybeans were two percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 32 percent fair, 44 percent good and10 percent excellent.
Seventy-two percent of the sorghum crop was coloring, 11 days ahead of last year's average of 57 percent, but slightly behind the average pace of 73 percent.
Sorghum was two percent very poor, eight percent poor, 34 percent fair, 45 percent good and 11 percent excellent.

Forty-eight percent of the cotton crop was opening bolls, compared with 35 percent a year ago and 30 percent average. Cotton was one percent very poor, 11 percent poor, 30 percent fair, 52 percent good and six percent excellent.
